newsitem.title: INDIA: India state seeks federal aid to fight extremists.
newsitem.headline: India state seeks federal aid to fight extremists.

text.p: India's southern state of Andhra Pradesh asked the federal government on Monday for 2,000 paramilitary troopers and 400 million rupees to tackle militancy, a state minister said.

Andhra Pradesh Home (Interior) Minister Madhava Reddy told reporters that Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu would meet Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Home (Interior) Minister Inderjit Gupta in New Delhi on Tuesday to press the request.
The state wants to upgrade its weapons and communications equipment in order to fight the extremists effectively, officials said.

A senior police official and his wife died on Monday when their vehicle hit a landmine which police said was planted by a group of left-wing extremists who killed 14 people in a daring attack last week.
The mine exploded as the van drove over a culvert, killing deputy police superintendent Mahesh Kumar and his wife, and injuring three other policemen, police officer K.L. Reddy told Reuters.

Police said the landmine was planted by the outlawed People's War Group (PWG), the same Maoist rebels who killed 13 policemen and a civilian last Friday in a raid on a police station in the Adilabad coal mining district of Andhra Pradesh.

Monday's explosion occurred at 6:30 a.m. (0100 GMT) near Ranapur town, 130 km (80 miles) east of the state capital Hyderabad. Last Friday's attack took place in Sirpuru village, 260 km (160 miles) from the capital.
The PWG is one of many Maoist rebel groups considered part of the Naxalite movement, which started in India in the 1960s among groups who split from the main communist party.
It was first banned in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 but gained a year-long reprieve beginning in June 1995 before being banned again in July of this year.
